catalog_quote: In the phonological word, stress (indicated in examples by ['] preceding the stressed syllable) is manifested by increased intensity and rising pitch on the stressed syllable. Stress falls on the penultimate syllable of bisyllabic roots, and remains on the root in monosyllabic roots. Stress does not move to the new penultimate syllable when affixes are added as is the case in Indonesian. Therefore, because stress is predictable it is considered to be non-phonemic in Luang.
